notes.1: Six ovenproof crocks or bowls on a sheet pan.

move.title: Reduce, caramelize, gratinée
move.body: French onion soup is two slow reductions: a beef stock cooked down by half until it's deep and full, and onions cooked for an hour until they collapse into a mahogany jam. You'll measure the reduction, deglaze the onions as they brown, combine and simmer, then float toasted bread and Gruyère on each bowl and broil it.

why.title: Reduce by half
why.body: Simmering a stock uncovered drives off water, concentrating flavor and gelatin. Measure: 10 cups to 5. Reduce before salting, since salt concentrates too.

why.title: Low and slow onions
why.body: Onions need about an hour over medium-low heat to caramelize. Rushed on high heat, they scorch at the edges while staying sharp inside.

why.title: Deglaze as you go
why.body: When a brown fond builds on the pot, a splash of water lifts it into the onions. Repeating this gives the soup its dark color.

why.title: The gratinée
why.body: Cheese on toast, floated on the soup and broiled close to the heat, melts and browns in 2 to 4 minutes. Watch it the whole time.

wrong.sign: The onions burned black in spots
wrong.fix: The heat was too high. Pick out the burned bits and lower the heat; deglaze more often.
The stock wasn't reduced enough. Simmer it uncovered 15 minutes more.
The broth was salted before reducing. Use low-sodium broth, and thin with water.

choices: Salt concentrates as the water evaporates

quiz.q: How long do the onions take to caramelize?

choices: Lifts the brown fond into the onions
quiz.explain: A splash of water each time.

steps.text: Simmer the broth with the bay and thyme in the saucepan, uncovered, until reduced by half. Measure it: 5 cups.
steps.look: Darker, and coats a spoon lightly.

steps.text: Halve the onions and slice them pole to pole ⅛ inch thick.
Melt the butter in the large pot over medium heat. Add the onions and salt and cover until they wilt.
Uncover, lower to medium-low, and cook, stirring every few minutes. Each time a brown fond builds, add a splash of the water and scrape it up.
Add the reduced stock to the onions, scrape the pot well, and simmer. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches below. Slice the baguette ¾ inch thick and toast the slices on the sheet pan until dry and golden on both sides.
Set the crocks on the sheet pan, ladle in the soup, float a toast on each, and pile on the cheese.
Broil until the cheese bubbles and browns in spots.
steps.tip: Stay at the oven; it goes from golden to burnt in seconds.

steps.text: Check the soup under the cheese.
Set each crock on a plate to serve. The crocks stay very hot for a long time.

toast.text: Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches below. Break the matzah into pieces that fit the crocks and toast them on the sheet pan until golden in spots.
toast.tip: Matzah browns in seconds under the broiler. Stay at the oven.

assemble.text: Set the crocks on the sheet pan, ladle in the soup, float the matzah pieces on each, and pile on the cheese.
